title: Cleaning the sky map
hook: Explore the evidence behind a cosmic question.

knows: Light and gravity help astronomers study the universe.
doesNotKnow: Microwave observations contain signals from the Milky Way and other foreground sources in addition to the CMB. Analysis attempts to separate these contributions.

misconception: A learner may choose: The CMB occurs only in front of the Moon
objective: Use the visual model to reason about: Why must scientists account for foreground emission when studying the CMB?

claims.text: Question, correct answer and explanation: Why must scientists account for foreground emission when studying the CMB? Our galaxy and other sources add signals to the sky. Microwave observations contain signals from the Milky Way and other foreground sources in addition to the CMB. Analysis attempts to separate these contributions.
Visual caption: Foreground + cosmic signal. The SVG is a conceptual illustration, not measured data or a scale model.

recall.question: Why must scientists account for foreground emission when studying the CMB?
options: The CMB occurs only in front of the Moon
Foregrounds make the universe stop expanding
Our galaxy and other sources add signals to the sky
recall.why: Microwave observations contain signals from the Milky Way and other foreground sources in addition to the CMB. Analysis attempts to separate these contributions.
